pathway.title: MAGNITE, INC. — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: Leverage and maturities leave creditors a wide cushion. Total debt is 1.76x reported EBITDA, down from 4.94x at the end of FY2024, cash exceeds debt, liquidity is 1.61x debt, and the nearest maturity is the undrawn revolver in 27 months, with the term loan 51 months away. Free cash flow before working-capital changes plus cash interest covers scheduled interest and amortization 6.38x, so debt service is a small claim on cash generation, and the only financial covenant is a springing leverage test that applies only when more than 35% of the revolver is drawn. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_mgni-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mgni-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; calculation B06; calculation B14; calculation B15; calculation B12

Free cash flow is genuine but flattered by working capital. Free cash flow before working-capital changes was 80.68% of reported EBITDA over the last twelve months and 112.58% after them, because working-capital inflows were 21.36% of operating cash flow. The inflow comes from amounts owed to sellers, which rise with volume and reverse if volume falls, so the cash flow that can service debt in a downturn is better measured before working capital. Capital expenditure is 9.54% of revenue after a step-up in FY2025, and the annual report expects investing outflows to fall in 2026, although maintenance and growth spending are not split. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_mgni-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 106; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mgni-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 51; calculation B01; calculation B02; calculation B03; calculation B04

Earnings quality is the main gap between headline and conservative leverage. The issuer states only an adjusted EBITDA, and reported EBITDA, calculated from the statements, is 70.94% of it because stock-based compensation makes up most of the add-backs. Leverage is 1.76x on the reported basis and 1.25x on the adjusted basis, so low leverage holds on either basis, but the adjusted figure overstates the cushion. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation B05

Business risk is the weakest dimension. The issuer generally has no long-term contracts with buyers or sellers, two buyers owed 40% and 12% of receivables at year-end FY2025, and connected-television inventory is held by a small number of large sellers with significant negotiating leverage, so the loss of one large seller or a fee concession could cut Contribution ex-TAC faster than costs adjust. The mechanism is the take rate: it is lower on connected television and in reserve auctions, connected television is 53% of revenue, and sellers and new entrants are building their own reserve-auction technology. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_mgni-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 35; 10-K_2025-12-31_mgni-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 41; 10-K_2025-12-31_mgni-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 43; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mgni-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 11

Cash balances are a poor guide to liquidity because they are matched by seller payables and swing with the season. The excess of seller payables over receivables equals 65.56% of cash and the fourth quarter carried 28.76% of FY2025 revenue; even a complete unwind of the excess, which the balances so far do not suggest, would leave liquidity at 0.87x total debt and above scheduled debt service. In a buyer default the issuer may still be required to pay sellers, so a collection failure would draw on cash before it reduces revenue. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_mgni-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 51; calculation B08; calculation B16; calculation B10; calculation B11

Near-term momentum is supportive but partly cyclical. Contribution ex-TAC grew 20% in Q3 2026 with connected television up 39%, management guides full-year growth of about 17%, and the midpoint of the Q4 guidance implies 17.92% growth on the prior-year quarter; but political advertising is now expected at nearly three times the initial forecast, and management's 2027 outlook is growth of over 15% excluding political and 10% on a total reported basis, so part of the 2026 growth will not repeat. These are management statements, not contracted revenue. Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-04_a991-earningsq32026.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_a991-earningsq32026.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation B18

Financial policy is moderate and cash-funded, and ownership is not established. Repurchases and share settlement taxes took 68.80% of nine-month free cash flow against 52.16% in FY2025, no priming or debt-funded distribution is described, and no controlling holder is named, which holds sponsor and governance risk at Medium. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A)

cells.text: Management describes Magnite as the world's largest independent omni-channel sell-side advertising platform and the largest independent programmatic connected television (CTV) marketplace, and the issuer also operates the SpringServe CTV ad server. This is management language.
Scale claim is management's own; larger competitors (Google, Facebook, Comcast and Amazon) hold more resources, so pricing power with sellers and buyers is limited.
CTV USD 108.785 million (53%, against 49% in Q3 2025), mobile USD 67.917 million (33%) and desktop USD 27.494 million (14%); total USD 204.196 million.
CTV is the largest and fastest-growing channel, so cash flow follows connected television advertising demand.
CTV USD 105.368 million (52.52% of the total), mobile USD 67.807 million and desktop USD 27.453 million; total USD 200.628 million, up 20% on the year, with CTV up 39%.
Contribution ex-TAC is revenue after traffic acquisition costs and is the measure the issuer uses to compare growth across channels.
United States USD 151.702 million (74%) and International USD 52.494 million (26%); 75% and 25% in FY2025.
Three quarters of revenue follows United States sellers, so the United States advertising cycle drives results; the split is by the location of sellers, not buyers.
Revenue reported on a gross basis was USD 5.856 million in Q3 2026 (3% of revenue) against 11% in Q3 2025 and 10% of FY2025 revenue; the rest is reported net.
Fewer gross-basis campaigns lower reported revenue but not Contribution ex-TAC, so revenue growth understates the underlying trend.

The annual report says the take rate, the fee as a share of advertising spend, tends to be lower on CTV transactions and on reserve auctions than on other channels and may decrease. Management language.
Growth concentrated in the lowest-fee channel can raise spend faster than revenue; the rate is not disclosed, so the effect cannot be sized.
Magnite generally has no long-term contracts with buyers or sellers; buyers are billed monthly and payment terms are generally seventy-five days or less.
Short contracts and short collection terms limit revenue visibility but keep the working-capital cycle short.

Two buyers were 40% and 12% of accounts receivable at 2025-12-31 (46% and 11% at 2024-12-31); one seller was 27% of accounts payable and accrued expenses (28% a year earlier); no seller reached 10% of revenue.
A dispute with the largest buyer would hit collections; one seller carries a concentrated payables balance.
Revenue, cash flow and operating results are expected to be higher in the fourth quarter than in other quarters because advertisers weight budgets to the holiday period.
Interim cash generation understates the year, and interim ratios against full-year figures are not like for like.

Management guides Q4 2026 Contribution ex-TAC of USD 227 million to USD 233 million and, for 2027, top-line growth of over 15% excluding political advertising and upside from the Google remedies, or 10% on a total reported basis. Management language.
Guidance is management's own view and excludes the Google litigation upside; it is not an assumption in this review.

runs.text: The credit strengths are these. Leverage is low and falling: total debt is 1.76x reported EBITDA, cash exceeds debt, and the term loan matures in 51 months, so refinancing pressure is distant and a shock would meet a balance sheet that does not need the market. Cash generation covers debt service 6.38x before working-capital changes, which leaves room for returns and investment without borrowing. Connected television is growing fastest, with Contribution ex-TAC up 39% in Q3 2026 against 5% for mobile and desktop combined, and the gross margin has widened from 61.26% in FY2024 to 66.62% over the last twelve months, so growth is converting into earnings. Financial policy has been creditor-neutral to supportive, with the convertible notes repaid from cash and no priming or debt-funded distribution. Disclosure is timely and audited with effective internal control. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); EX-99.1_2026-11-04_a991-earningsq32026.htm.jsonl, page 1; calculation B12; calculation B15; calculation B19; calculation B20

The credit weaknesses are these. Revenue is not contracted: there are generally no long-term contracts, which limits visibility to the next few quarters and makes results sensitive to advertiser budgets. Counterparties are concentrated: two buyers owed 40% and 12% of receivables, and connected-television sellers are few and large, so one relationship can move earnings. The take rate is exposed to mix and competition, because it is lower on connected television and in reserve auctions, and the competitors named in the annual report are larger. Reported EBITDA is 70.94% of the adjusted figure and working capital supplies 21.36% of operating cash flow, so the cash flow that can be relied on in a downturn is smaller than the headline. Ownership is not established and shareholder returns are rising as a share of free cash flow, which holds governance risk at Medium. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_mgni-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-K_2025-12-31_mgni-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 35; 10-K_2025-12-31_mgni-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 41; 10-K_2025-12-31_mgni-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 43; calculation B05; calculation B03

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: No sponsor transaction, leveraged buyout, merger or new financing is described in the supplied documents. The transaction facts that bear on creditors are the repayment of the convertible notes at maturity in March 2026, the repurchase plan approved in February 2026, a revolver draw and repayment within the second quarter of 2026, and a third repricing of the term loan on October 7, 2026, after the September 30 balance sheet date. Basis: 10-Q_2026-03-31_mgni-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mgni-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 50; 10-Q_2026-06-30_mgni-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mgni-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 29

There has been no new debt issue in 2026 to date. The last new-money facilities were the February 2024 refinancing, a USD 365.0 million term loan due February 2031 and a USD 175.0 million revolver due February 2029, secured by substantially all assets; the October 2026 amendment changes pricing only, cutting the term loan margin by 50 bp to Term SOFR plus 2.50% and the revolver margin range to 2.50% to 3.00%. The 0.25% convertible notes, issued in March 2021 at USD 400.0 million, no longer exist after the March 15, 2026 repayment of USD 205.1 million from cash. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_mgni-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mgni-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 29; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mgni-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-K_2025-12-31_mgni-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 64

The only acquisition with cash paid in the annual cash flow statements from FY2023 and in 2026 is Streamrai, Inc. in September 2025, for total consideration of USD 10.1 million, of which USD 8.1 million was paid in cash and USD 2.0 million was held back against indemnification claims. The transformational acquisitions of SpotX and SpringServe were in 2021, and the SpotX cash consideration was financed in part by the term loan and the convertible notes. No transaction in the supplied documents has a stated sponsor, purchase multiple or pro forma leverage. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_mgni-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 145; 10-K_2025-12-31_mgni-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-K_2025-12-31_mgni-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 121; 10-K_2025-12-31_mgni-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 63; 10-K_2025-12-31_mgni-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 84

fields.value: Financial foundation for MAGNITE, INC. (issuer id mgni) as of 2026-11-05 on the credit snapshot pathway: statements, debt, liquidity and credit metrics for FY2024, FY2025 and the last twelve months to 2026-09-30, taken from the supplied annual report, quarterly reports and earnings releases.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Magnite is lightly levered at September 30, 2026: total debt of USD 349.95 million is 1.76x LTM reported EBITDA, cash exceeds debt, and the term loan balloon is not due until February 2031, so the main creditor exposure is earnings quality and seller float.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Reported EBITDA is derived from the statements because the issuer states only an adjusted figure; on the adjusted basis leverage is 1.25x and interest cover is 10.98x, against 7.79x on the reported basis, and stock-based compensation is most of the difference. Operating cash flow includes a working-capital inflow and seller payables exceed receivables, so not all of the cash balance is free liquidity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage has fallen sharply because debt was repaid and EBITDA grew. Total debt over reported EBITDA was 4.94x at the end of FY2024, 3.88x at the end of FY2025 and is 1.76x on the last twelve months to September 30, 2026; on issuer-adjusted EBITDA the ratios are 2.81x, 2.40x and 1.25x. Net debt of USD 70.525 million at the end of FY2024 became USD 2.75 million at the end of FY2025 and net cash of USD 42.912 million at September 30, 2026, because free cash flow exceeded share repurchases and the taxes paid on share settlement. The repayment of the USD 205.067 million convertible notes in March 2026 used cash and debt in equal amounts, so it lowered gross leverage without materially changing net debt, and the FY2025 total debt figure includes USD 204.815 million of notes that no longer exist. Interest cover on reported EBITDA improved from 3.04x in FY2024 to 5.09x in FY2025 and 7.79x on the last twelve months, as EBITDA grew and cash paid for interest fell after the term loan margin was cut in September 2024 and March 2025.

The working-capital line is driven by seller payables, which are the largest liability on the balance sheet at USD 1,689,794 thousand at September 30, 2026 against receivables of USD 1,432,233 thousand, so cash less the excess of payables to sellers over receivables is USD 135,301 thousand. The excess was USD 217,734 thousand at the end of FY2024, USD 270,148 thousand at the end of FY2025 and USD 257,561 thousand at September 30, 2026, so the float is large and broadly stable; the issuer states that it may still have to pay sellers if a buyer defaults, so a buyer default or slow collection would draw on cash before it reduces revenue.

fields.value: Liquidity is ample against near-term obligations: cash of USD 392.862 million and USD 170.9 million available under the USD 175.0 million revolver give USD 563.762 million against debt of USD 349.95 million, and the revolver was drawn and repaid for USD 60.0 million within the second quarter of 2026 without leaving a balance. Scheduled term loan amortization is USD 3.632 million a year, the balloon of USD 342.294 million is due in February 2031 and the revolver commitment ends in February 2029, so no facility expires within twelve months. The only financial covenant is a springing first-lien net leverage test that applies when more than 35% of the revolver is used; the ratio is not printed, so headroom is not calculated here.

fields.value: Two events sit outside the period figures. On October 7, 2026, after the balance sheet date, Amendment No. 3 cut the term loan margin by 50 bp to Term SOFR plus 2.50% and lowered the revolver margin range to 2.50% to 3.00%; it changes cash interest, not debt or cash, and is not blended into any period figure. The 0.25% convertible notes matured on March 15, 2026, and that repayment has several figures with different roles: principal paid of USD 205.067 million in the cash flow statement, net carrying value of USD 204.815 million at the prior year-end on the balance sheet, and an estimated fair value of USD 199.2 million at that date. Carrying value serves the leverage figures, principal serves the cash flow and the maturity history, and fair value serves no ratio.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: EBITDA is the main definitional risk. The issuer states only Adjusted EBITDA, so reported EBITDA is calculated from income before tax, net interest and depreciation and amortization; the issuer's add-backs total USD 81.541 million over the last twelve months, 90.31% of which is stock-based compensation, so the adjusted ratios are materially better than the reported ones. Total debt uses carrying value of USD 349.95 million, USD 7.78 million below principal, and USD 61.994 million of lease liabilities sit on their own lines outside debt. No pension, retiree, factoring or supplier finance obligation is disclosed in any source. Cash paid for interest of USD 25.549 million exceeds net interest expense of USD 19.696 million because net expense is after USD 9.251 million of interest income.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Business, ownership, governance and transaction fact review of MAGNITE, INC. (issuer id mgni) as of 2026-11-05 on the credit snapshot pathway. It covers the company and operating model, ownership and control, shareholder returns and debt behaviour, and the dated history of the issuer, taken from the supplied annual report, quarterly reports and earnings releases. No sponsor transaction, acquisition or new debt issue is being underwritten in the supplied documents.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The supplied filings name no sponsor, parent or controlling shareholder, and documented behaviour toward creditors is neutral to supportive, so sponsor and governance risk is Medium, held there mainly by missing ownership evidence.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Shareholder returns are covered by free cash flow but appear to be rising: repurchases and share settlement taxes took 68.80% of free cash flow in the nine months to September 30, 2026, against 52.16% in FY2025. The larger creditor exposure is the business itself: connected television is 53% of revenue, the issuer generally has no long-term contracts with buyers or sellers, and two buyers owed 40% and 12% of receivables at year-end FY2025.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No controlling holder is named, but the filings do not rule one out. The annual report defers its ownership and board items to a proxy statement that is not among the supplied documents, so the only ownership fact is about 42 holders of record at February 19, 2026, and holders in street name are not counted. Takeover defences, including a classified board, removal of directors only for cause by a supermajority vote, no action by written consent and the Delaware business-combination statute, make a hostile change of control harder; that protects management continuity, but no change-of-control protection for creditors can be read because the credit agreement is not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Shareholder returns are the main discretionary use of cash and are paid from operating cash flow. Magnite has never declared a dividend and the credit facility restricts them, but a repurchase plan approved on February 23, 2026 allows up to USD 200.0 million through February 29, 2028, of which USD 55.1 million had been used and USD 144.9 million remained at September 30, 2026. Repurchases plus taxes paid on net share settlement were 68.80% of free cash flow in the nine months to September 30, 2026, up from 52.16% in FY2025; repurchases alone were 44.57%. The revolver was undrawn at September 30, 2026, although the purpose of the second-quarter draw is not stated, so the mechanism is a smaller cash cushion, not higher debt, and the nine-month ratio is likely to fall as seasonally strong fourth-quarter cash flow arrives.

fields.value: Behaviour toward lenders has been neutral to supportive. The 2021 acquisition of SpotX was financed in part with a term loan and USD 400.0 million of convertible notes; the issuer bought back USD 194.9 million of the notes in 2023 for USD 165.5 million, a 15.08% discount, and repaid the remaining USD 205.1 million at maturity on March 15, 2026 from cash. The term loan was refinanced in February 2024 to mature in February 2031 and has since been repriced three times, the last on October 7, 2026 after the balance sheet date, cutting the margin by 200 bp in total to Term SOFR plus 2.50%; repricing hands value to the borrower but no priming, uptier, drop-down or non-pro-rata transaction is disclosed. A USD 60.0 million revolver draw in the second quarter of 2026 was repaid within the quarter.

fields.value: The business is a connected-television-led sell-side platform with short revenue visibility and a take rate that depends on mix. Connected television was 53% of revenue and 52.52% of Contribution ex-TAC in Q3 2026 and its Contribution ex-TAC grew 39% on the year, but the annual report says the take rate is lower on connected television and on reserve auctions than elsewhere, so spend can grow faster than revenue. The issuer generally has no long-term contracts with buyers or sellers, advertiser budgets weight the fourth quarter, and 74.29% of Q3 revenue comes from the United States.

fields.value: Counterparty concentration sits on the buyer side and in one seller balance. Two buyers accounted for 40% and 12% of accounts receivable at December 31, 2025, together 52%, against 46% and 11% a year earlier, and one seller accounted for 27% of accounts payable and accrued expenses, although no seller reached 10% of revenue. The buyers and the seller are not named, so the credit quality behind the largest balances cannot be tested.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Disclosure quality is adequate for monitoring, with one transition to track in finance leadership. The annual report carries an unqualified audit opinion from Deloitte, the auditor since 2018, and effective internal control over financial reporting; no material related-party transactions were reported, and insider trading and clawback policies are filed. The Chief Financial Officer changed between the second and third quarter reports under a transition agreement dated April 17, 2026, with the successor previously the Chief Accounting Officer, and senior officers adopted pre-arranged trading plans for share sales in the third quarter; the terms of the transition are not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Litigation against Google is an option on market share, not a base-case cash source. The court found Google liable on April 17, 2025, Magnite filed its own action on September 16, 2025, and in September 2026 the court issued a remedies opinion with a six-year compliance monitor that Google intends to appeal; management's outlook for 2027 growth of over 15% excludes any upside from the remedies, against 10% on a total reported basis.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a Medium rating is favourable: free cash flow in the nine months to September 30, 2026 comfortably covers the return programme, debt has been repaid rather than added, and the only change to lender terms on record is repricing in the borrower's favour. A Low rating becomes arguable once the proxy statement shows dispersed ownership and independent oversight and the credit agreement shows restricted payments that are bounded.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence for a worse view is the direction of returns: they rose from 52.16% of free cash flow in FY2025 to 68.80% in the nine months to September 30, 2026, USD 144.9 million of authority remains, and the baskets that would limit further returns are not in the supplied documents. The view would move to High if returns were funded by revolver borrowing, if a controlling holder with distribution rights emerged, or if any exchange, priming or asset-transfer transaction appeared; the first observable warning would be returns that exceed free cash flow for a full year.

fields.value: Overall, Magnite presents Medium sponsor and governance risk. The key supported behaviour is cash-funded shareholder returns alongside full repayment of the convertible notes from cash, which matters because it keeps debt falling while using free cash flow that could otherwise build liquidity, and implies stable creditor treatment for as long as returns stay within free cash flow. Countervailing evidence is the repricing of the term loan in the borrower's favour, which lowers lender yield without changing priority. Further analysis requires the proxy statement and the credit agreement. This governance review is completed with limitations, and the sponsor and governance risk level is Medium.

fields.value: No sponsor transaction, leveraged buyout, merger or new financing is described in the supplied documents. The transaction facts that bear on creditors are the repayment of the convertible notes at maturity in March 2026, the repurchase plan approved in February 2026, a revolver draw and repayment within the second quarter of 2026, and a third repricing of the term loan on October 7, 2026, after the September 30 balance sheet date.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: There has been no new debt issue in 2026 to date. The last new-money facilities were the February 2024 refinancing, a USD 365.0 million term loan due February 2031 and a USD 175.0 million revolver due February 2029, secured by substantially all assets; the October 2026 amendment changes pricing only, cutting the term loan margin by 50 bp to Term SOFR plus 2.50% and the revolver margin range to 2.50% to 3.00%. The 0.25% convertible notes, issued in March 2021 at USD 400.0 million, no longer exist after the March 15, 2026 repayment of USD 205.1 million from cash.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The only acquisition with cash paid in the annual cash flow statements from FY2023 and in 2026 is Streamrai, Inc. in September 2025, for total consideration of USD 10.1 million, of which USD 8.1 million was paid in cash and USD 2.0 million was held back against indemnification claims. The transformational acquisitions of SpotX and SpringServe were in 2021, and the SpotX cash consideration was financed in part by the term loan and the convertible notes. No transaction in the supplied documents has a stated sponsor, purchase multiple or pro forma leverage.

fields.value: Sponsor / Governance Risk Level: Medium. The level is driven by missing ownership evidence and a rising, cash-funded return programme, because these leave the control and distribution risk unconfirmed, which implies monitoring posture rather than a change in the credit view. Countervailing evidence is cash repayment of debt, a 2031 maturity and the absence of any exchange or priming transaction.

fields.value: Fundamental credit review of MAGNITE, INC. (issuer id mgni) as of 2026-11-05 on the credit snapshot pathway: business risk, financial profile, outlook, downside path and monitoring triggers. It builds on the supplied annual report, third quarter report and earnings release and on the earlier source readiness, financial and business reviews. It assigns no rating and sizes no position.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Magnite is a sound credit for a leveraged-finance issuer, with net cash, liquidity of 1.61x debt and no maturity before 2029, but its earnings rest on uncontracted advertising demand, so the main risk is a cash-flow shock, not leverage.

fields.value: Free cash flow before working-capital changes was 80.68% of reported EBITDA over the last twelve months, but reported EBITDA is only 70.94% of the issuer's adjusted figure and the excess of seller payables over receivables equals 65.56% of cash, so the cushion is thinner than headline net cash suggests.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage and maturities leave creditors a wide cushion. Total debt is 1.76x reported EBITDA, down from 4.94x at the end of FY2024, cash exceeds debt, liquidity is 1.61x debt, and the nearest maturity is the undrawn revolver in 27 months, with the term loan 51 months away. Free cash flow before working-capital changes plus cash interest covers scheduled interest and amortization 6.38x, so debt service is a small claim on cash generation, and the only financial covenant is a springing leverage test that applies only when more than 35% of the revolver is drawn.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Free cash flow is genuine but flattered by working capital. Free cash flow before working-capital changes was 80.68% of reported EBITDA over the last twelve months and 112.58% after them, because working-capital inflows were 21.36% of operating cash flow. The inflow comes from amounts owed to sellers, which rise with volume and reverse if volume falls, so the cash flow that can service debt in a downturn is better measured before working capital. Capital expenditure is 9.54% of revenue after a step-up in FY2025, and the annual report expects investing outflows to fall in 2026, although maintenance and growth spending are not split.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Earnings quality is the main gap between headline and conservative leverage. The issuer states only an adjusted EBITDA, and reported EBITDA, calculated from the statements, is 70.94% of it because stock-based compensation makes up most of the add-backs. Leverage is 1.76x on the reported basis and 1.25x on the adjusted basis, so low leverage holds on either basis, but the adjusted figure overstates the cushion.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Business risk is the weakest dimension. The issuer generally has no long-term contracts with buyers or sellers, two buyers owed 40% and 12% of receivables at year-end FY2025, and connected-television inventory is held by a small number of large sellers with significant negotiating leverage, so the loss of one large seller or a fee concession could cut Contribution ex-TAC faster than costs adjust. The mechanism is the take rate: it is lower on connected television and in reserve auctions, connected television is 53% of revenue, and sellers and new entrants are building their own reserve-auction technology.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_mgni-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 35; 10-K_2025-12-31_mgni-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 41; 10-K_2025-12-31_mgni-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 43; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mgni-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash balances are a poor guide to liquidity because they are matched by seller payables and swing with the season. The excess of seller payables over receivables equals 65.56% of cash and the fourth quarter carried 28.76% of FY2025 revenue; even a complete unwind of the excess, which the balances so far do not suggest, would leave liquidity at 0.87x total debt and above scheduled debt service. In a buyer default the issuer may still be required to pay sellers, so a collection failure would draw on cash before it reduces revenue.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Near-term momentum is supportive but partly cyclical. Contribution ex-TAC grew 20% in Q3 2026 with connected television up 39%, management guides full-year growth of about 17%, and the midpoint of the Q4 guidance implies 17.92% growth on the prior-year quarter; but political advertising is now expected at nearly three times the initial forecast, and management's 2027 outlook is growth of over 15% excluding political and 10% on a total reported basis, so part of the 2026 growth will not repeat. These are management statements, not contracted revenue.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial policy is moderate and cash-funded, and ownership is not established. Repurchases and share settlement taxes took 68.80% of nine-month free cash flow against 52.16% in FY2025, no priming or debt-funded distribution is described, and no controlling holder is named, which holds sponsor and governance risk at Medium.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against the favourable view is that the business has no contractual backlog: results depend on advertiser budgets and seller choices that can change within a quarter, and part of the cushion is seller payables that can reverse. Four signals would move the view toward caution: Contribution ex-TAC below the low end of the Q4 guidance of USD 227 million, payables to sellers no longer exceeding receivables, revolver use above 35%, or a fee concession by a large seller.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence for a more favourable view is financial: cash is 1.12x debt, debt service is covered 6.38x before working-capital changes, and there is no maturity for 27 months. Growth in Contribution ex-TAC at or above the 17% guided for FY2026 with stable seller payables, and a springing covenant that stays unused, would support a stronger view of business risk.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The credit strengths are these. Leverage is low and falling: total debt is 1.76x reported EBITDA, cash exceeds debt, and the term loan matures in 51 months, so refinancing pressure is distant and a shock would meet a balance sheet that does not need the market. Cash generation covers debt service 6.38x before working-capital changes, which leaves room for returns and investment without borrowing. Connected television is growing fastest, with Contribution ex-TAC up 39% in Q3 2026 against 5% for mobile and desktop combined, and the gross margin has widened from 61.26% in FY2024 to 66.62% over the last twelve months, so growth is converting into earnings. Financial policy has been creditor-neutral to supportive, with the convertible notes repaid from cash and no priming or debt-funded distribution. Disclosure is timely and audited with effective internal control.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The credit weaknesses are these. Revenue is not contracted: there are generally no long-term contracts, which limits visibility to the next few quarters and makes results sensitive to advertiser budgets. Counterparties are concentrated: two buyers owed 40% and 12% of receivables, and connected-television sellers are few and large, so one relationship can move earnings. The take rate is exposed to mix and competition, because it is lower on connected television and in reserve auctions, and the competitors named in the annual report are larger. Reported EBITDA is 70.94% of the adjusted figure and working capital supplies 21.36% of operating cash flow, so the cash flow that can be relied on in a downturn is smaller than the headline. Ownership is not established and shareholder returns are rising as a share of free cash flow, which holds governance risk at Medium.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Magnite runs a sell-side advertising platform that connects publishers, mainly connected-television, mobile and desktop sellers, with advertising buyers through auctions and direct deals, and it earns a fee that is generally a percentage of the advertising spend it transacts, with most revenue reported net. Connected television is 53% of revenue in Q3 2026, and about three quarters of revenue follows United States sellers. The model supports debt service through a short cash cycle, since buyers are billed monthly on terms generally of seventy-five days or less, but it weakens revenue visibility because there are generally no long-term contracts, advertiser budgets weight the fourth quarter, and counterparties are concentrated. The history that matters to creditors is the 2021 acquisition of SpotX, financed in part with debt that has since been repaid or refinanced, and the 2024 refinancing that moved the term loan to February 2031.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_mgni-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-K_2025-12-31_mgni-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 43; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mgni-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mgni-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mgni-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Magnite is a listed Delaware corporation, and the supplied filings name no sponsor, parent or controlling holder; holders above any threshold are not established because the proxy statement is not supplied. A classified board and supermajority provisions make a hostile takeover harder, which lowers event risk but gives creditors no change-of-control protection that can be read. The borrower is the listed company itself, and the senior secured facilities are secured by substantially all assets of the company and its guarantor subsidiaries, which are not named, so claims ranking ahead at subsidiary level cannot be assessed. Financial policy has been cash-funded: repurchases and share settlement taxes took 68.80% of nine-month free cash flow, no dividend has ever been paid, and no exchange, priming or drop-down is described.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is transactional and discretionary: fees depend on advertising spend, impression volume, price and mix, and on a take rate that is lower on connected television and in reserve auctions than on other channels. Connected television drives growth, with Contribution ex-TAC up 39% in Q3 2026, but connected-television inventory sits with a few large sellers that have negotiating leverage, buyers can press for fee concessions, and sellers and new entrants are building their own reserve-auction technology, so pricing power is limited. The issuer generally has no long-term contracts, so revenue is predictable only as far as the guided quarter, and the managed-service business that reports gross is down to 3% of revenue, which lowers reported revenue but not Contribution ex-TAC. Revenue is also exposed to substitution by seller-owned technology and direct buyer-seller connections, and to identity and privacy changes that could favour platforms with first-party data.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margins have widened with scale: gross margin rose from 61.26% in FY2024 to 66.62% over the last twelve months, operating expenses fell from 53.62% to 48.15% of revenue, and reported EBITDA margin rose from 16.77% to 25.96%. The cost base is partly committed: non-cancelable cloud, software and data-center obligations equal 29.33% of cash and 15.03% of last-twelve-month revenue, and management states that the business has many fixed costs, so volume growth lifts profit disproportionately and a fall in Contribution ex-TAC would compress margins faster than costs could be cut. The split between fixed and variable cost is not disclosed, so resilience is judged from the expense lines and commitments available.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital intensity is moderate: capital expenditure is 9.54% of revenue and free cash flow before working-capital changes is 80.68% of reported EBITDA, so earnings convert to cash after interest and capital spending. Interest is a small claim, equal to 12.84% of reported EBITDA, and the term loan margin has been cut by 200 bp in total since 2024. Working capital is not dependable: its inflow was 21.36% of operating cash flow, driven by seller payables, and seasonality puts 28.76% of revenue in the fourth quarter. Maintenance and growth capital expenditure are not split, so flexibility over the maturity wall is inferred from the annual report's expectation that investing outflows will fall in 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_mgni-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 106; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mgni-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 29; calculation B04; calculation B01; calculation B13; calculation B03; calculation B16

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Competitive rivalry is high: Google, Facebook, Comcast and Amazon are named as larger competitors with greater resources, which keeps fees under pressure and ties margin durability to share. The threat of new entrants is moderate and rising in reserve auctions, where new entrants and sellers building their own technology can lower fees. The threat of substitutes comes from sellers connecting directly with demand-side platforms or buyers and from walled gardens with first-party data, which would cut volume through the platform. Buyer power shows in requests for fee concessions and in two buyers owing 40% and 12% of receivables, so collection and pricing risk is concentrated. Seller power is high in connected television, where a few large sellers hold negotiating leverage, may demand guarantees or minimum spend commitments, and are consolidating, so the loss of one relationship could cut revenue and cash flow quickly.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Regulatory, economic and technological factors are material to credit quality; social factors do not appear to be a primary credit driver on the provided materials. On regulation, the court found Google liable in April 2025 and issued a remedies opinion in September 2026 with a six-year compliance monitor that Google intends to appeal, which management expects to help its display business but which is excluded from its outlook, and the issuer is subject to privacy class action lawsuits; the effect on cash flow is not established. On the economy, advertising is cyclical, political advertising is intermittent and unpredictable, and 2026 benefits from political spending now expected at nearly three times the initial forecast, so 2027 growth is guided at 10% on a reported basis against over 15% excluding political. On technology, cookie deprecation and the shift to first-party data change competitive position and may require the platform to be re-engineered at significant cost.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths: low leverage with net cash, liquidity above total debt, maturities that begin in 2029, debt service well covered, and connected-television growth. Weaknesses: uncontracted revenue, counterparty concentration, exposure of the take rate to mix, reported EBITDA well below the adjusted figure, and ownership that is not established. Opportunities that could improve credit quality: a shift of connected-television sellers toward biddable auctions, which carry a higher take rate, and any Google remedy that widens display share. Threats that could weaken it: consolidation of connected-television sellers, seller-built reserve-auction technology, a drop in advertiser budgets, and identity changes that favour larger platforms.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The main supports are low leverage (1.12x cash to debt and 1.76x debt to reported EBITDA), liquidity of 1.61x debt, and debt service covered 6.38x before working-capital changes; the main constraints are uncontracted revenue, concentration, a float that supports cash, and a reported EBITDA that is 70.94% of the adjusted figure. The trend is improving: total debt to reported EBITDA fell from 4.94x at the end of FY2024 to 3.88x at the end of FY2025 and 1.76x on the last twelve months, and interest cover rose from 3.04x to 7.79x. The key missing datapoints are the credit agreement, a forward model, peer benchmarks and the take rate by channel.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation B07; calculation B06; calculation B12; calculation B05

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over the next 12 months to 24 months the tailwinds are connected-television growth, with the Q4 guidance midpoint implying 17.92% growth, political advertising that is nearly three times the initial forecast in 2026, and lower interest cost after the October 2026 repricing; the headwinds are the roll-off of political spending, which the 2027 outlook reflects with 10% growth on a reported basis against over 15% excluding political, and fee pressure in reserve auctions. Over the medium term of three to five years the tailwind is a possible shift of connected-television sellers to biddable auctions with higher take rates, and the headwinds are seller consolidation, seller-built technology and identity changes. Refinancing falls inside the medium term, with the revolver due in 27 months and the term loan in 51 months, so the low leverage and cash generation will matter when the facilities are extended. All outlook figures are management statements, not contracted revenue.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The realistic downside starts with an advertising slowdown while a large connected-television seller consolidates into a competitor or presses for lower fees. The first operational break is a fall in Contribution ex-TAC through lower volume and a lower take rate, while many costs are fixed, operating expenses equal 48.15% of revenue and committed obligations do not adjust quickly. The financial transmission is lower EBITDA and operating cash flow, and a reversal of the working-capital inflow as payables to sellers fall with volume: the excess of seller payables over receivables equals 65.56% of cash, and a complete unwind would leave liquidity at 0.87x total debt. Leverage would rise as EBITDA fell, and the springing covenant would apply only if more than 35% of the revolver were drawn; the revolver falls due in 27 months and would need extending during the downturn. Management can suspend the repurchase plan at its discretion, and repurchases with share settlement taxes took 68.80% of nine-month free cash flow, and it can slow capital expenditure, so resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress in a one-year downside, with no default assumed. The observable triggers are Contribution ex-TAC below the Q4 guidance, payables to sellers no longer exceeding receivables, and revolver use.
